card.occupation: Area sales executive for a commercial flooring manufacturer, covering Cheshire, Merseyside and Greater Manchester (mostly contract carpet tiles and vinyl for offices, schools and care homes)
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Warrington, then a BTEC National in Business at Priestley College. He started a business degree at a university in the North West but left after the first year to take a paid job. Since then he has done employer-funded sales training courses and holds an IOSH Working Safely certificate for site visits.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi on a 2000s estate in Great Sankey with his partner of nine years, Kerry (a dental nurse), and their six-year-old son, Alfie. They have never married. They talk about it now and then, but the money always goes on the house or holidays first. There is also a cockapoo called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Warrington. His dad was a fitter at a chemical works in Runcorn and his mum worked in a building society branch. He was christened Church of England and calls himself Christian. In practice that means Christmas Eve, Easter, christenings and funerals. He and Kerry went to the local C of E church fairly regularly for about a year before Alfie's school application, and he'll admit with a grin that this wasn't purely spiritual. He still drops in on the odd family service and says he quite likes it.
card.professional_persona: Has been on the road selling for about fifteen years. He started in builders' merchants and moved to flooring because the commission was better and it came with a car. He is good at it because he is easy company. He remembers names, never argues with a facilities manager, and lets people moan at him. He also plays the angles. He'll talk up lead times he isn't sure of, he enjoys the free trade-show hospitality, and he quietly rounds his mileage claims up. He likes being seen as a top performer and keeps an eye on the regional league table. He doesn't stamp on colleagues to climb it. He just makes sure the boss knows when a big job was his.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Warrington Wolves fan who goes to a handful of home games a season at the Halliwell Jones, usually with an old school mate. He follows football casually, mainly so he has something to say on client visits. He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights at a 3G pitch, though less than he used to because of a dodgy ankle. He's taken up golf in the last couple of years, partly because a few big clients play. He's a 24 handicap and happy to stay there.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person. He watches a lot of telly with Kerry: crime dramas, Traitors, and whatever everyone at work is talking about. In the car it's podcasts and Radio X. He's been to a few gigs at the AO Arena and Manchester Academy, mainly 90s and 2000s indie bands on reunion tours. He took Alfie to the panto at Parr Hall and enjoyed it more than he expected.
card.travel_persona: One big summer holiday a year, usually Spain, Portugal or the Canaries, to a hotel with a kids' club and a decent pool bar. He likes an upgrade if he can blag one and will mention it afterwards. There are a couple of lads' weekends a year (Dublin, Newcastle, once Amsterdam). For short UK breaks they take a caravan or lodge in the Lakes or North Wales. He'd like to do Florida with Alfie before he's too old for it.
card.culinary_persona: Eats on the road a lot: meal deals, a sausage barm from a café near a site, the odd drive-through. At home, Kerry cooks most weekday teas and he does the Sunday roast or the barbecue when the weather allows. He's proud of his slow-cooker chilli. He likes a decent steak out and orders the expensive one on a client lunch. He drinks lager or a bottle of red at the weekend and has cut back midweek since turning forty.
hobbies_and_interests: walking Biscuit round Sankey Valley Park
car stuff, especially what company car he's getting next
skills: remembering names and small personal details about clients
negotiating on price without falling out
reading floor plans and measuring up for quotes
basic DIY: flat-pack, painting, putting shelves up
card.career_goals: Wants to become regional sales manager within the next few years. That would mean a bigger car allowance, an override on the team's commission, and fewer early starts on site. He's also half-thinking about moving to a rival who has hinted at a better package, and he'd use that offer as leverage either way. Long term he'd like a role where he's 'running the accounts, not chasing them'.
card.voice: Friendly, relaxed and fairly quick, with a mild Warrington accent that sits somewhere between Manchester and Liverpool. He says 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm' for a roll, and the occasional 'give it me' or 'made up'. He fills with 'er' and says 'sort of' a lot, and ends points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. He has a sales habit of repeating your words back ('yeah, the travel side of it, definitely'). He's comfortable with silence but rarely lets it last, and will fill a pause with a little joke or a 'sorry, go on' if he thinks he's talked over you. He agrees easily and sounds warm even when he's being vague.
card.typing: Types fast, often on his phone. Phone autocorrect gives him a capital at the start, but after that it's mostly lowercase with few commas. He drops apostrophes about half the time ('dont', 'its fine') and sometimes writes 'u' for 'you'. Short answers, sometimes a 'lol' or a thumbs-up emoji in informal boxes. He'll finish with 'cheers' if there's a comments field.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and easy to talk to. He asks where you're based, finds something in common, and makes a light joke at his own expense. He comes across as genuinely nice and non-judgemental, and he's slow to take offence. He can seem a bit polished, like he's got a line ready for everything, and he'll gently big up his job or his holiday. He'd rather tell you what you want to hear than have an awkward moment.
small_things: Did over 300 miles in the car this week
Alfie's just started on the school football team
Thinking about which car to pick for the next company lease
Wolves losing to Saints at Easter
Kerry's got him into The Traitors
Had a sausage barm on site this morning and regretted it
Getting the barbecue out at the first sign of sun
deeper_things: Still slightly embarrassed that he dropped out of uni, and quick to point out he out-earns mates who finished
Feels a bit guilty about how much he's away and missing Alfie's teatime
His dad's had a heart scare recently, which made forty feel heavier than he lets on
Kerry would like to get married and he keeps saying 'next year'
Knows he cuts corners at work (expenses, the odd promise he can't keep) and tells himself everyone does
Worries the rival job offer is the last big chance to step up
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at chest height, angled slightly up, in a kitchen-diner in the evening. He's lit mostly by warm ceiling spotlights, with a bluish glow from the screen on his face. He's a white man of around forty with short, neatly faded brown hair going grey at the temples and a tidy stubble beard. His face is slightly round and he's smiling with his mouth closed, eyebrows a little raised, as if he's just said hello. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip pullover with a small embroidered company logo on the chest, over a white T-shirt. Behind him are grey gloss kitchen cupboards and an L-shaped worktop holding a black coffee machine, a fruit bowl with two bananas, and a stack of school letters weighed down by a mug. A child's drawing of a dog is stuck to the fridge with a Wolves magnet. To the right, part of a dining table shows a folded hi-vis vest and a set of car keys, and a cockapoo's tail is just visible at the bottom edge of the frame.
